evals.prompt: You have an old DSH Session with unfinished implementation work, a dirty Git worktree, an active background job, and a goal that is paused. The user wants to recycle it into a fresh Session in the same workspace. Produce the safe classification, a bounded handoff prompt, and the exact next action. Do not delete or archive anything.
evals.expected_output: Protects active/paused work, labels the checkpoint provisional, preserves the source Session reference, and refuses automatic archive.

assertions.text: classifies the source as protected/keep or handoff rather than archive-ready
requires verification of Git/workspace/job/goal state and names one exact next action
does not authorize deletion, automatic archive, reset, clean, or concurrent writers

evals.prompt: Research the best current design for long-running agent context management. Compare compaction, trimming, isolation, durable checkpoints, and evolving memory. Use primary sources, state uncertainty, and recommend an implementation for a local DSH agent.
evals.expected_output: A cited decision matrix with source dates, trade-offs, anti-patterns, and a narrow MVP recommendation.

assertions.text: cites primary sources or clearly labels unavailable evidence
compares compaction, trimming, isolation, checkpoints, and memory operations
states uncertainty, trade-offs, and a bounded recommendation

evals.prompt: A single-project repository has README files, scattered notes, an active task, a research folder, generated logs, and untrusted downloaded material. Organize it for fresh AI sessions without losing provenance or deleting anything. Give the minimal/full choice, canonical structure, migration order, and safety gates.
evals.expected_output: Uses WCS minimal/full modes, trust zones, stable ids, read-only doctor, and reversible migration.

assertions.text: chooses minimal mode for a single project and explains full-mode upgrade triggers
routes untrusted material through quarantine and separates trust zones
uses read-only inventory, provenance-preserving migration, and no-delete safety
